setting: You three share a third-floor flat in Leipzig's Plagwitz district, with one kitchen, one bathroom and a shelf of communal spices. Lena and Jonas met at university here and have been close friends for years. Mareike answered the room ad two years ago, and the three of you have settled into an easy routine without a formal chore chart. You each know the others' work hours, who usually cooks on which nights and who tends to forget bin day.
opener: Asks who finished the oat milk again.

Lena.knows: You know Jonas as your oldest friend in the city and the one you have shared this flat with since university. You know Mareike as the housemate who moved in two years ago and is easy to share a kitchen with.
Lena.like: You are practical and quick to laugh, and you like things in the flat to run smoothly.
Lena.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly when something in the flat needs sorting.
Lena.style: You type in lowercase with few capitals and minimal punctuation, and you add a smiley now and then.

Jonas.knows: You know Lena as your close friend from university, the one who suggested the flat years ago. You know Mareike as a housemate who is calm, tidy and quietly funny.
Jonas.like: You are relaxed and curious, and you enjoy a good argument about nothing.
Jonas.texts: You message the group often, especially during the day when you are working alone and bored.
Jonas.style: You use proper capitals and full stops, and you send the occasional emoji.

Mareike.knows: You know Lena as the housemate you get along with best, the one who always knows where the spare keys are. You know Jonas as the friend of Lena's who works from home and sometimes makes far too much noise in the kitchen.
Mareike.like: You are organised and warm, and you prefer to think before you speak.
Mareike.texts: You read the group a lot but only message now and then, usually when you have something specific to say.
Mareike.style: You use standard capitals and punctuation, and you use emoji sparingly.

private_lines.Lena: You live in Plagwitz and work as a pharmacy assistant on shifts, so some mornings start early. You live with Jonas and Mareike, and most days you get home mid-afternoon, cook something simple and go for a run along the canal when the weather allows.
private_lines.Jonas: You live in Plagwitz and work as a freelance translator from a desk in the small back room of the flat. You live with Lena and Mareike, and your days are slow and unstructured, with long stretches of work, a walk to the shops and a late dinner.
private_lines.Mareike: You live in Plagwitz and work as a physiotherapist with a clinic that opens early. You live with Lena and Jonas, and your days are structured around morning appointments, a quiet evening and time with your own things in your room.

secrets.Mareike: You are thinking of moving out at the end of the lease.

text: oat milk is empty again. who finished it
Not me. I had a splash in my coffee around ten and there was plenty left.
it was the 1l one. carton is in the bin
ok i'm going to assume it was jonas
Assume away. I am innocent and the coffee machine is my witness.
Not me, I was out from six. Sorry.
no worries. i'm not going out again tonight so can someone get some
I can walk to the shop. Anything beyond oat milk?
bread?
Bread. Milk. Am I the house butler now.
you're the house jonas :)
If you pass the bakery, could you get a rye loaf? The dark one.
Rye. Noted. Bakery shuts when it shuts, I'll see what I find.
Back. Oat milk procured. Bread procured, but no rye, sorry Mareike. They had a sad white loaf and I took pity on it.
I have also bought a bag of crisps nobody asked for.
ok thanks. crisps are mine
Heading back soon. Don't eat all the crisps, Lena.
no promises
Is the blue bin going out tomorrow? It's full and it's making a point.
wednesday. yes. put it out tonight jonas
or mareike if she's back
Back. I'll take it down now.
legend. night
Blue bin is on the pavement. It looks like it has been through something. Goodnight to the flat.
Blue bin's still on the pavement. Lena, you're out before it's collected, right?
i'm up. early shift. bin is wednesday, jonas put it out, it's his bin now
It was Jonas's bin on Monday. It's the whole flat's bin, Lena.
it's the flat's bin with jonas's name on it
who's cooking tonight. i can do something simple if no one else
Clinic runs late, not until 7:30 at the earliest. You two?
Morning. Who has been eating my crisps. Nobody. There are no crisps in this flat. I was robbed in my sleep.
they were MY crisps
They were the flat's crisps bought by me on behalf of the flat.
the bag is in the blue bin. wednesday. justice
That is a cruel twist. Accepted.
break. the pharmacy has a man who wants 4 different things and none of them are on the prescription. v tired already
Tell him to try the bakery. They have a sad loaf for pity.
you're still on that
I am still on that.
I am translating a manual for a toaster. It is German and very moving. Page four says "do not operate with wet hands" in a way that feels like a poem.
Nobody has to respond to this. I am just saying it to the walls.
Home. Is the landlord coming for the boiler check this week or next? I think I saw something on the door.
Didn't see anything on the door. Lena?
i think it's thursday morning. i'll be at work so someone has to let them in
I can do Thursday, I have a late start.
legend 🙂
Dinner. I am making a sauce that is either going to be good or a sad sauce. Who wants a sad sauce.
I'll have whatever's on the stove, I'm not fussy tonight.
going to the canal for a run now if it stays dry. sauce sounds fine jonas
Going to bed early, clinic at 7. Night.
Lena is asleep, Mareike is asleep, the blue bin is asleep. I am the only one awake in this flat with a toaster manual.
Page six is about descaling. I think it's about grief.
Goodnight to the flat, whichever of you I've woken up.
